text: In the Timaeus, how does Plato famously define time (chronos)?
choices: As a moving image of eternity, proceeding according to number
As the number of motion with respect to before and after
As the rational measure, or Logos, of an ever-changing fire
As the empty void in which eternal atoms move and recombine
explanation: At Timaeus 37d Plato defines time as 'a moving image of eternity, proceeding according to number' - the Demiurge's numbered, cyclical likeness of the changeless eternal model. Option 1 is Aristotle's later definition in the Physics; option 2 is Heraclitus' Logos; option 3 is the Atomists' void. Only the first is Plato's.
